note: The literature confirms a broad phenotypic spectrum in NKX6-2-related disorder ranging from severe neonatal-onset global psychomotor delay to childhood-onset spastic ataxia with preserved cognitive function.

evidence.text: Chelban et al. (2020) characterize the NKX6-2 phenotypic spectrum as spanning from severe global psychomotor delay at the severe end to a childhood-onset predominantly motor phenotype with relatively preserved cognition at the milder end.

source.title: Genetic and phenotypic characterization of NKX6‐2‐related spastic ataxia and hypomyelination
source.quote: Our data reveal a phenotype spectrum with neonatal onset, global psychomotor delay and worse prognosis at the severe end and a childhood onset with mainly motor phenotype at the milder end.

evidence.text: In the initial 2017 report by Chelban et al., affected individuals were noted to have normal cognitive function rather than universal moderate-to-severe impairment, though other reports associate the gene with severe intellectual disability.

source.title: Mutations in NKX6-2 cause progressive spastic ataxia and hypomyelination
source.quote: His cognitive function was within normal range; he achieved ten top GCSE school grades.
